name: REF5040IDR
title: REF50xx low-noise, low-drift precision series voltage reference family (2.048 V to 10 V)
summary: A family of band-gap series references with fixed outputs from 2.048 V to 10 V that both source and sink up to 10 mA. Three grades: enhanced (REF50xxEI, 2.5 ppm/°C, 0.025 %, 0.5 µVPP/V noise, up to 42 V in, with enable), high (REF50xxI, 3 ppm/°C, 0.05 %) and standard (REF50xxAI, 8 ppm/°C, 0.1 %), the last two to 18 V with a trim and noise-reduction pin. A TEMP pin gives a voltage proportional to die temperature. SOIC-8 and VSSOP-8, specified from -40 °C to 125 °C. REF5040IDR is the 4.096 V, high-grade SOIC-8 part on tape and reel.
key_figures: VOUT + 0.2 V to 42 V (EI), to 18 V (I, AI)

pins.name: TEMP
pins.function: Voltage that rises with die temperature, about 2.64 mV/°C, from roughly 60 kΩ source impedance.

pins.name: TRIM/NR

pins.name: EN

circuits.title: REF5040 as the reference of a 16-bit ADC
circuits.description: An OPA365 wired as a unity-gain follower buffers a 0 V to 4 V signal into the positive input of an ADS8326 through a 124 Ω and 1 nF RC filter; the negative input is grounded. A REF5040 running from 5 V, with 1 µF on its input, drives the converter's REF pin, which carries 22 µF to ground.

circuits.title: Buffered TEMP output
circuits.description: A low-drift op amp, run from the same +V as the reference, follows the TEMP pin so a load does not pull its high-impedance output; the buffer output gives about 2.6 mV/°C. OPA333, OPA335 or OPA376 are the amplifiers named for it.

circuits.title: Noise reduction capacitor on TRIM/NR
circuits.description: A 1 µF capacitor from TRIM/NR to ground forms a low-pass filter with the internal resistors, corner about 10 Hz to 20 Hz, roughly halving the output noise and lengthening start-up.

circuits.title: Output adjustment through TRIM/NR
circuits.description: A 10 kΩ potentiometer in series with 2 kΩ hangs from VOUT to ground; its wiper feeds TRIM/NR through 1 MΩ, moving the output by about ±15 mV. REF50xxI and REF50xxAI only.

circuits.title: Basic connections
circuits.description: The minimum circuit: a 1 µF to 10 µF bypass capacitor on VIN and an output capacitor CL from VOUT to ground. CL is 1 µF to 50 µF for REF50xxI and REF50xxAI and 1 µF to 100 µF for REF50xxEI; its ESR must be 1.5 Ω or less, and 1 Ω to 1.5 Ω gives the lowest noise.

parts.value: 1 µF to 50 µF (REF50xxI, REF50xxAI); 1 µF to 100 µF (REF50xxEI)

circuits.title: ±2.5 V references from a REF5025 and an OPA735
circuits.description: A REF5025 on +5 V gives +2.5 V with 1 µF to ground. An OPA735 inverting stage with two matched 10 kΩ resistors, its non-inverting input grounded and its supplies at +5 V and -5 V, turns that into -2.5 V. The two resistors need matching temperature coefficients. Supply bypass capacitors are not part of this circuit.

circuits.title: 16-bit, 250 kSPS data acquisition system
circuits.description: A REF5040 drives the REFIN pin of an ADS8326. Its output carries 10 µF to ground and a 47 µF capacitor in series with a resistor (ESR) to ground; an output capacitor with too low an ESR causes gain peaking that lowers the system SNR. An OPA365 follower drives the converter input from a 0-4 V signal through 124 Ω and 1 nF.

parts.note: series resistance for the 47 µF capacitor, no value given

notes: SNR 86.7 dB with 10 µF on the output and no TRIM/NR capacitor; 92.8 dB with 10 µF + 47 µF and 1 µF on TRIM/NR.

operation.text: Three grades share the family. REF50xxEI (enhanced, SOIC-8 only, 2.5 V to 5 V options) runs from up to 42 V, draws at most 480 µA and has an enable pin; REF50xxI (high) and REF50xxAI (standard) run to 18 V, draw up to 1.2 mA and bring out TRIM/NR in place of EN and NR.

A band-gap core buffered to the output. On REF50xxI and REF50xxAI the band-gap node reaches TRIM/NR through an internal 10 kΩ (R4) and 1 kΩ (R3) network, and TEMP comes from a 10 µA (at 25 °C) temperature-proportional current into 60 kΩ. On REF50xxEI the same TEMP source uses 62 kΩ, the NR pin sits on the band-gap filter and EN switches the device.

TEMP gives a voltage rising 2.64 mV/°C, good to about ±15 °C, useful for tracking temperature changes or compensating analog circuits. Its source impedance is high (about 60 kΩ), so a low-impedance load shifts the reading; the load has no effect on VOUT. A low-drift op amp follower removes the loading error.

0.1 Hz to 10 Hz noise rises with output voltage and with temperature. Filtering after the output lowers it, provided the added output impedance does not hurt. On REF50xxI and REF50xxAI, 1 µF from TRIM/NR to GND sets a 10 Hz to 20 Hz pole with the internal resistors and roughly halves output noise; more capacitance lowers the corner further, and any capacitor there lengthens start-up.

REF50xxI and REF50xxAI are trimmed at the factory; TRIM/NR (pin 5) allows a further adjustment of about ±15 mV using a 10 kΩ potentiometer and 2 kΩ divider from VOUT, with the wiper reaching TRIM/NR through 1 MΩ.

VIN needs a bypass capacitor: 1 µF to 10 µF in the basic connection, placed close to the VIN and GND pins (0.1 µF to 10 µF for REF50xxEI, smallest closest to the part); add more for noisy or high-impedance supplies. VOUT needs a capacitor to GND for stability: 1 µF to 50 µF (REF50xxI, REF50xxAI) or 1 µF to 100 µF (REF50xxEI). On REF50xxI and REF50xxAI its ESR must be no more than 1.5 Ω, with 1 Ω to 1.5 Ω best for noise; a resistor in series with the capacitor may supply it. REF50xxEI wants a low-ESR output capacitor, 1 Ω at most. Too low an ESR causes gain peaking and raises noise in an ADC system.

Unloaded, the supply only needs to be 200 mV above VOUT, except the REF5020, which needs at least 2.7 V. Under load the dropout grows with load current. Supply bypass is 1 µF to 50 µF for REF50xxI and REF50xxAI and 1 µF to 100 µF for REF50xxEI.
EN above 1.6 V, or left floating, runs the reference; below 0.5 V the output is off and the device draws about 10 µA.

The output sources and sinks up to 10 mA across the input range; the short-circuit current is about 25 mA (REF50xxI, REF50xxAI) or 21 mA (REF50xxEI). Self-heating follows TJ = TA + PD × θJA, and TJ must not exceed 150 °C.

Unequal thermal expansion of the package materials stresses the die when it is heated, and reflow can shift the output voltage and the drift. In a test of 36 parts reflowed once with lead-free paste on 0.8 mm, 13 mm × 13 mm FR4 boards, the shifts were small, but larger boards or different thickness or material can shift more, and each further reflow adds shift. On a board reflowed twice, the reference is best placed in the last pass.

Bypass capacitor (1 µF to 10 µF) as close as possible to VIN and GND. 1 µF from TRIM/NR to ground for noise filtering. Output decoupled with 1 µF to 50 µF, ESR 1 Ω to 1.5 Ω for best noise (a series resistor is optional), plus a 1 µF high-frequency capacitor in parallel at the output to filter noise and handle switching loads such as data converters.

Bypass capacitor (0.1 µF to 10 µF) as close as possible to VIN and GND, smallest nearest the part. 0.1 µF to 1 µF class 1 capacitor from NR to ground. Output decoupled with 1 µF to 100 µF, ESR 1 Ω or less.
